003ccbf4ca3f631a.title: Combinatorial tools for posets topology and simplicial complexes
003ccbf4ca3f631a.speaker: Lucas Pouillart
003ccbf4ca3f631a.abstract: Topological theory of posets originates from a simple observation : the Möbius function of an interval of a poset P can be interpreted as the Euler characteristic of a simplicial complex. It turned out that in a lot of cases, these complexes hold a lot more information on P and that a lot of interesting examples satisfy the (homotopy) Cohen-Macaulay property, which gives both nice topological and algebraic properties. A lot of techniques were developed by combinatorialists to prove the Cohen-Macaulay property and give interpretations of algebraic and topological problems for posets as enumeration problems, and I will present some of them in this talk.

0167472cc5f71f0e.title: Fuzzy Sphere Meets CFT: 3D Ising, Fermions and Gauge Theories
0167472cc5f71f0e.speaker: Yin-Chen He
0167472cc5f71f0e.abstract: In this series of lectures, I will introduce the "fuzzy (non-commutative) sphere regularization," a recently proposed non-perturbative approach to 3D CFTs. I will first elucidate its fundamental concepts and then dive into illustrative examples, including the 3D Ising transition, fermionic CFTs, and Chern-Simons matter theories. I will comment on the potential theoretical direction in understanding fuzzy sphere regularization from the aspect of algebra on fuzzy sphere.

0320d26b64efe087.title: Height pairing over arithmetic function fields
0320d26b64efe087.speaker: Juan Felipe Castro-Cardenas
0320d26b64efe087.abstract:
Since the foundational work of Néron and Tate in the 60s, various conjectural definitions of the height pairing for homologically trivial algebraic cycles on smooth, projective varieties over a number field, or more general global fields, have been proposed by Belinson, Bloch, Gillet-Soulé and Schneider, among others. The related concept of height functions on sub-varieties was extensively developed by Faltings and, in the early 2000s, extended by Moriwaki to varieties defined over finitely generated extensions of $\mathbb{Q}$, also called arithmetic function fields. More recently, Bruno Kahn has used algebraic intersection theory to give a geometric construction of a ``refined" height pairing over the function field of a smooth, projective variety $B$, taking its values in $\textrm{Pic}(B)$.
In this talk, I will present an Arakelov-geometric analogue of this construction over an arithmetic function field $K$, taking its values in the arithmetic Picard group of a normal arithmetic variety whose function field is $K$. The construction is in two parts: first, Kahn's definitions are extended and adapted to arithmetic varieties using the intersection theory on regular schemes of Gillet-Soulé, and then the Archimedean term is added by considering generalized Green currents satisfying some ``admissibility" conditions, inspired by the original work of Arakelov. If time allows, I will discuss the connection with Moriwaki's work and with the work of Brosnan and Pearlstein on the degeneration of the Archimedean height pairing.

05360b5228778ddf.title: Automath! À qui appartiennent les mathématiques ? Maths + IA Controversy Workshop
05360b5228778ddf.abstract:
À qui appartiennent les mathématiques ? En deux ans à peine, les mathématiques semblent être passées du statut de frontière de l’IA à celui de territoire de l’IA, du statut d’idéal cognitif servant à tester les capacités de raisonnement des modèles d’IA, à celui d’infrastructure de connaissance, productive et mobilisable de façon en partie automatisée. C’est en tous cas le message envoyé par OpenAI (e.g. Contre-exemple à la conjecture d’Erdős), Anthropic (e.g. Contre-exemple à la conjecture jacobienne), Google DeepMind (e.g. AlphaProof) ou encore la DARPA avec le programme ExpMath. Si le moment se veut historique, la suite n’est pas écrite pour autant. La communauté mathématique se prépare et s’interroge : À quel endroit faut-il résister ? Et à quel autre faudrait-il plutôt s’adapter ? À quelles conditions ? Comment souhaitons-nous voir se dessiner les trajectoires de l’IA et de la recherche mathématiques ? L’équipe Inria SIRA, le LFPC et le collectif Automath invitent la communauté mathématique élargie à se saisir collectivement de ces enjeux lors d’une journée de workshop (ai4sciencecontroversy.com)
Comme en témoigne la Déclaration de Leiden [1.] ou le formule Terence Tao dans une publication récente [2.] : « How should the mathematical community respond to the advent of modern AI technologies, and their real and/or claimed capabilities to perform mathematical tasks? (…) It is a metamathematical question. »

06382073817a5fcb.title: Les polygraphes réguliers et leur théorème de recollement homotopique
06382073817a5fcb.speaker: Clémence Chanavat
06382073817a5fcb.abstract:
Je commencerai par présenter deux (ou trois) manières de régulariser les polygraphes, que j'appellerai méthode-Hadzihasanovic, méthode-Steiner et, si le temps le permet, méthode-Henry.
J'expliquerai pourquoi la méthode-Hadzihasanovic ne produit pas toujours des polygraphes, à moins que l'on impose aux ∞-catégories strictes des lois d'échange supplémentaires, dictées par des égalités de topologie combinatoire.
Je terminerai par un théorème de recollement, issu de mes derniers travaux, qui assure que certains de ces polygraphes sont librement générés en un sens homotopique, ce qui signifie que ce sont aussi des polygraphes dans la théorie des (∞, n)-catégories.

0ce8f3485edf456e.title: The Messy Story of Crossing Dispersion Relations
0ce8f3485edf456e.speaker: Andrea Guerrieri
0ce8f3485edf456e.abstract:
In this talk I will discuss an attempt of unifying under a simple geometric picture, the plethora of crossing symmetric dispersion relations existing in literature.
Each dispersion is valid on a different finite window in energy, but none of them could be extended to infinity.
I will explain how they can all be understood from a simple choice of a foliation of the kinematics space.
This geometric viewpoint also suggests the existence of a particular (but not so nice) foliation that naturally covers all energies. Unfortunately, this example turns out to be impractical for phenomenological and bootstrap applications. I will comment why, and what teaches us about the dual bootstrap.

0d498cd40a8129cc.title: Autour de la localisation des racines d’un polynôme après dérivation
0d498cd40a8129cc.abstract:
Dans cet exposé nous étudierons plusieurs questions autour du problème de la localisation des racines d’un polynôme dérivé par rapport aux racines de ce polynôme.
Tout d’abord nous rappellerons quelques résultats déterministes classiques autour de ce problème. Puis nous étudierons ce problème sous un angle probabiliste en nous demandant où se situent les racines du polynôme dérivé lorsque les racines du polynôme initial ont été tirées de manière indépendante et identiquement distribuée dans le plan complexe. Pour finir, nous étudierons ce problème sous un angle d’analyse en expliquant comment ce dernier peut mener à l’étude d’une équation aux dérivées partielles non linéaire et non locale obtenue après passage à une limite champ moyen
.

1015b3e268727771.title: Condensed homotopy types in algebraic geometry, arithmetic geometry, and logic
1015b3e268727771.speaker: Peter Haine
1015b3e268727771.abstract:
Let X be a locally topologically noetherian scheme. In their paper on the proétale topology, Bhatt and Scholze defined the proétale fundamental group π1proét(X). The profinite completion of π1proét(X) recovers the usual étale fundamental group. Moreover, π1proét(X) agrees with π1ét(X) when X is normal, but π1proét(X) has the better property that it classifies Qp-local systems. In this talk, we’ll explain how to use condensed mathematics to define a “condensed homotopy type” whose fundamental group refines the proétale fundamental group. We’ll also talk about two related “condensed homotopy types”: one for adic spaces and one in the setting of logic. All three are special cases of a more general invariant of ∞-topoi. For adic spaces, the fundamental group refines the de Jong fundamental group, and in logic, the fundamental group recovers the Lascar group of a complete first-order theory.
These results come from several projects, carried out jointly with Holzschuh–Lara–Mair–Martini–Wolf, Achinger–Holzschuh–Lara–Mair–Wolf, and Damaj–Zhang.

108bbe056f400b03.title: Advances in Quantum Cryptography, Paris
108bbe056f400b03.abstract:
This is a thematic trimester programme with short courses, seminars and workshops on mathematical developments in Advances in Quantum Cryptography (QCRYPTO).
September 13th to December 10th, 2027 at the Institut Henri Poincaré, Paris
** REGISTRATION IS MANDATORY AND FREE **
Deadline for financial support request is March 15, 2027
Presentation of the programme
Quantum cryptography lies at the intersection of cryptography, quantum information, and computational complexity. Quantum technologies offer new cryptographic possibilities, while also changing our understanding of which security guarantees and computational tasks are achievable. Recent developments have revealed deep connections between these areas, but many fundamental questions remain open.
This programme will bring together researchers from theoretical computer science, mathematics, cryptography, and quantum information. It will explore three closely connected directions: information-theoretic foundations, including quantum communication, nonlocality, randomness, and device-independent security; complexity-theoretic foundations, including quantum proofs, verification, reductions, and computational assumptions; and computational and interactive primitives, including commitments, zero knowledge, secure computation, and protocols involving quantum devices.
Through an introductory school, seminars, focused workshops, informal discussions, and extended research visits, the programme aims to develop a common language across neighboring communities. It will provide opportunities for sustained collaboration between senior and junior researchers, encourage new research partnerships, and help identify important directions for the next stage of quantum cryptography.

11bdf66a7d726fe3.title: 2-catégories de fusion graduées par les 3-groupes et invariants quantiques homotopiques
11bdf66a7d726fe3.speaker: Matthew Cellot
11bdf66a7d726fe3.abstract:
À la fin du XXe siècle, les travaux remarquables de Jones, Drinfeld,
Witten et Kontsevich ont permis la construction de nouveaux invariants de
variétés, appelés invariants quantiques, obtenus notamment à partir de certains
groupes quantiques. L’un des premiers succès dans cette direction est l’invariant
de Turaev-Viro-Barrett-Westbury des 3-variétés, défini comme une somme d’états
à partir de la donnée d’une catégorie de fusion. Plus récemment, Douglas et
Reutter ont construit des invariants de 4-variétés par somme d’états, en utilisant
des 2-catégories de fusion.
Cet exposé porte sur les invariants quantiques homotopiques, c’est-à-dire les
invariants quantiques de variétés munies d’une structure supplémentaire codée
par une application vers un espace topologique. Plus précisément, nous
généralisons la construction de Douglas-Reutter pour obtenir des invariants des
3-fibrés plats sur les 4-variétés ou, de manière équivalente, des 4-variétés
munies d’une classe d’homotopie d’applications vers un 3-type d’homotopie.
Les structures algébriques utiles pour cette construction sont les 2-catégories
de fusion graduées par les 3-groupes, où le 3-groupe modélise le 3-type
d’homotopie. Dans ce cadre, les applications vers un 3-type d’homotopie sont
codées par des triangulations coloriées. En démontrant une généralisation
coloriée du théorème de Pachner, nous obtenons que ces invariants sont
indépendants de la triangulation choisie.

13761740d538d513.title: French-Japanese Conference on Arithmetic Geometry in Honor of Takeshi Saito and Takeshi Tsuji
13761740d538d513.abstract:
French-Japanese Conference on Arithmetic Geometry in Honor of Takeshi Saito and Takeshi Tsuji
May 31 - June 4, 2027 at IHES - Marilyn and James Simons Conference Center
How to get to IHES
This conference, which is part of a long-standing tradition of French-Japanese collaboration in arithmetic geometry, will honor two leading figures of this partnership: Professor Takeshi Saito, on the occasion of his retirement, and Professor Takeshi Tsuji, on the occasion of his 60th birthday.
The main topics of the conference will include:
p-adic Hodge theory, including the p-adic Simpson correspondence, geometric Sen theory, p-adic Galois representations and (φ,Γ)-modules, prismatic cohomology, and their applications;
Ramification theory, including singular support and characteristic cycles of l-adic étale sheaves (in equal and mixed characteristic), compatibility with proper higher direct images, Swan conductors, and epsilon-factors;
Geometric Langlands theory, l-adic, p-adic, and for modules with integrable connections, in characteristic p and in characteristic 0.

13e82dee4c5aba9f.title: Multi-scale modeling and analysis of signal processing in neurons
13e82dee4c5aba9f.speaker: Claire Guerrier
13e82dee4c5aba9f.abstract: In this talk, I will present models for signal propagation in neurons, ranging from the macro- to the micro-scale, with various applications to neuronal signalling. The first application concerns myelin plasticity, and the influence of neuronal myelin geometry on signal transmission. We investigate the evolution of the maximum of a signal in a damped heat equation on x>0, with a Dirichlet boundary condition representing the signal, which models signal transmission in a myelinated internode. We derive an expression of the solution, and derive the Dirichlet-to-Neumann operator at x=0. We then investigate the max. At a more refined scale, to investigate signal summation in the neuronal dendritic tree, we consider the Poisson-Nernst Planck system of equations representing ionic electrodiffusion in an electrolyte. This system expresses a sharp boundary layer of the size of the Debye length at the boundary, where the extra-charges accumulates. In particular, we derive an asymptotic approximation of the solution at steady state, in the regime of small Debye length.

166b8544bc7b6165.title: Mosquito borne disease outbreak : Climate change impact to Physics Informed Neural Network use
166b8544bc7b6165.speaker: Aniket Banerjee
166b8544bc7b6165.abstract:
Dengue, Zika and chikungunya are expanding across new
territories as their vector, the tiger mosquito _Aedes albopictus_,
tracks a warming climate. Forecasting where and when outbreaks will
occur requires models that are both mechanistically faithful to mosquito
ecology and disciplined by real observational data — yet the
biological parameters that govern transmission, such as the biting rate,
the extrinsic incubation period and mosquito survival, are precisely the
ones we cannot measure directly in the field.
In this talk, I present a national -scale furcating framework that
couples a mechanistic _Aedes albopictus_ population model, in the spirit
of the Arbocarto approach, to a vector-to-human transmission layer, and
the use of Neural Network use to predict diffusion pattern in
epidemiological systems. I will explain the modelling choices behind the
population and transmission layers, the structure of the inverse
problem, and how PINNs let a mechanistic model "speak" to messy,
heterogeneous data.

1b6482bf56f6c80c.title: Origami Tori
1b6482bf56f6c80c.speaker: Richard Schwartz
1b6482bf56f6c80c.abstract:
An origami torus is a piecewise affine isometric embedding of a flat torus into R3. It is surprising that these things exist, but thanks to the work of Burago and Zalgaller in 1960 they do. 30 years later, B&Z proved that every flat torus is realized as an origami torus. In 2023, Lazarus and Tallerie proved that you can realize all flat tori using a single underlying triangulation with about 2500 vertices.
The question remained: how many vertices do you need to make an origami torus? In this talk I will prove that the minimum number of vertices needed is 8. I will also discuss joint work, with Peter Doyle, proving that almost every flat torus is represented by an 8-vertex origami torus. Finally, I will explain work-in-progress with Doyle, Fabian Lander, and Steve Trettel, which shows that in fact every flat torus is represented by an 8-vertex origami torus. If I have time, I will also discuss hyperbolic versions of this business.

1f1458617ffc520d.title: Sur la probabilité qu’un entier possède un diviseur de la forme $p-1$ dans un intervalle donné
1f1458617ffc520d.speaker: Rebecca Abi Abdallah
1f1458617ffc520d.abstract: Dans cet exposé, nous étudierons la fonction qui compte les entiers naturels inférieurs ou égaux à $x$ possédant, dans un intervalle $(y,z]$, un diviseur de la forme $p-1$, où $p$ est premier. En analysant le comportement asymptotique de cette quantité dans les différents régimes de $z=z(y)$, nous mettrons en évidence une transition de phase qui révèle les dépendances entre ces événements de divisibilité en fonction de la longueur logarithmique de l’intervalle $(y,z]$. Notre résultat généralise un théorème de Ford correspondant au cas $z=x$. Ceci est un travail en collaboration avec V. Kovaleva, J. Schlitt et N. Tardy.

209c607116a6625d.title: Verso Blueprint: Reimagining Blueprints for the AI Era
209c607116a6625d.speaker: Emilio Gallego Arias
209c607116a6625d.abstract:
Large-scale formalization projects have long needed tools to
coordinate contributions, track dependencies, and connect mathematical
exposition with formal proofs. A key example is Lean
Blueprint. Introduced in 2020 for the sphere eversion project, Lean
Blueprint extends plasTeX to provide a shared map of statements,
dependencies, Lean declarations, and progress. Lean Blueprint's model
has been quite influential and has helped shape how mathematicians and
formalizers work together on large-scale formalization projects.
This talk presents recent work on Verso Blueprint, a Lean-native
implementation of the Lean Blueprint concept built on Verso, Lean's
official markup language. Designed for close integration with Lean,
Verso Blueprint maintains a three-layer database linking source
material, informal statements, and their formalized counterparts. The
database is populated from Verso documents, analysis of Lean
declarations, and other user-provided data. Interactive HTML views
provide navigation and previews, connecting mathematical exposition
with the formal development. We have now largely reached our original
goal, with functionality comparable to Lean Blueprint or Lean
Architect.
But matching that functionality is no longer enough: this is an
extraordinary moment for formalisation. The practice is radically
chaining even as we build its tools.
When we began this project, our central use case was for humans to
write detailed statements and dependencies to guide
formalization. Today, coding agents are increasingly writing and
interacting with the blueprints themselves in an autonomous
fashion. Blueprints are taking on the reverse role: not just guiding
the construction of formal proofs, but making AI-generated proofs
intelligible to humans. At the same time, dependency tracking and
organizational information remain essential for coordinating
large-scale autoformalization. For example, Prove2Me, a theorem
database with dependency tracking, played a key coordination role in
the recent Fermat's Last Theorem auto-formalization milestone.
What comes next for blueprints in this extraordinary moment? We are
redesigning Verso Blueprint around the idea of "programmatic
blueprints": human-readable, machine-actionable objects synchronized
with formal developments. Our ambition is for blueprints to become a
*foundational harness for AI-assisted formalization*, maintaining the
shared state of a project and coordinating what happens next across
mathematicians, formalizers, code repository workflows, and agents.

25f6fa5329055aa8.title: Dynamique de Aut(F_n) sur G^n, pour G compact et n grand
25f6fa5329055aa8.speaker: Serge Cantat
25f6fa5329055aa8.abstract:
Donnons nous un groupe de Lie compact G et un entier n.
Un n-uplet (g_1, …, g_n) étant donné, on peut changer l’un des g_i en son inverse, ou multiplier l’un des
g_i par g_j (avec j différent de i) : ces opérations élémentaires ne changent pas le sous-groupe de G
engendré par les g_i. Ces opérations engendrent un groupe de difféomorphismes de G^n, et le problème
que nous aborderons est d’étudier la dynamique de ce groupe. Pour n suffisamment grand, nous verrons
qu’il est possible de classer les fermés et les mesures invariants.

2c0d38068fdfcb8e.title: Conditions de stabilité à la Bridgeland et applications
2c0d38068fdfcb8e.speaker: Vanja ZULIANI
2c0d38068fdfcb8e.abstract:
Les conditions de stabilité à la Bridgeland nous permettent d’étudier les espaces de modules d’objets dans une catégorie dérivée et de décomposer chaque objet en facteurs plus “simples". Cette thèse examine deux applications de la théorie des conditions de stabilité à la Bridgeland. Dans la première partie, on étudie la géométrie d’une variété de Fano de dimension 8 et d’indice 3, définie comme une sousvariété lagrangienne d’une variété hyperkählérienne ; on étudie une dégénérescence semistable et on en déduit ses nombres de Hodge. En particulier, on observe que la structure de Hodge est de type K3 et que le rang de Picard est égal à un.
La deuxième application de la théorie des conditions de stabilité concerne l’étude du programme des modèles minimaux non commutatifs. On montre que les décompositions semiorthogonales standard sur les grassmanniennes, les quadriques et les hypersurfaces cubiques de dimension 3 et 4 sont induites par des chemins quasi-convergents dans la variété de stabilité, dont la charge centrale est donnée par la cohomologie quantique. Une partie du dernier chapitre est basée sur un travail en collaboration avec Tomohiro Karube et Antonios-Alexandros Robotis.

2fa116d313ddc82a.title: The Pentagram Map and Ramifications
2fa116d313ddc82a.abstract:
October 12-15, 2026
at IHES - Marilyn and James Simons Conference Center
How to get to IHES
This workshop explores the mathematics connected to the pentagram map and its generalizations.
With 3 talks per day, spread out over 4 days, leaving time for individualized interactions, it will not be confined to the special topic of the pentagram map, but rather an exploration of the kind of mathematics that it relates to: integrable systems, algebraic dynamics, projective geometry and cluster algebras.
The pentagram map is a geometrically flavored dynamical system defined on polygons by a simple and projectively natural straight-line construction.
Starting with a polygon, one intersects the shortest diagonals in cyclic order to produce a new polygon with the same number of vertices.
Though quite elementary to define, the pentagram map turns out to have a deep structure connected to completely integrable systems, symplectic geometry, cluster algebras, dimers, algebraic dynamics, and moduli spaces.
The same goes for the many generalizations of the pentagram map, some of which are still quite mysterious.

364676bd1455fdad.title: Équations diophantiennes et cohomologie galoisienne
364676bd1455fdad.abstract:
Le point de départ de cet exposé est d’expliquer comment classifier les surcorps non-commutatifs d’un corps K (par exemple, R a un surcorps non-commutatif donné par le corps des quaternions H, qui est de dimension 4 sur R).
L’idée clé derrière cette classification est la notion de « descente galoisienne » : informellement, elle consiste à dire que les objets définis sur un corps K viennent d’objets définis sur la clôture algébrique de K qui sont munis d’une action d’un certain groupe qu’on appelle le groupe de Galois absolu de K.
La classification de tels objets fait naturellement intervenir des groupes de cohomologie associés à ce groupe de Galois absolu, appelés groupes de cohomologie galoisienne. Ces groupes sont intimement liés aux propriétés diophantiennes du corps K : si certaines équations homogènes sur K avec beaucoup de variables ont des solutions, alors ces groupes de cohomologie ont tendance à s’annuler à partir d’un certain degré.
Pour rendre compte de ce phénomène, Lang a introduit la notion de corps C_i et a conjecturé que les corps C_i avaient une cohomologie triviale en degré > i. Cette conjecture est ouverte pour i>2 et on sait que sa réciproque est fausse. Si le temps le permet, je parlerai des conjectures de Kato et Kuzumaki qui raffinent la propriété C_i pour tenter d’avoir une condition diophantienne qui caractérise l’annulation de la cohomologie du corps en degré >i.

3725e6d2e1bc26a0.speaker: Jean-Philippe Burelle
3725e6d2e1bc26a0.abstract: Motivated by a family of examples constructed by R. Schwartz based on Pappus's theorem, we explore constructions of representations of discrete groups arising from incidence theorems in projective spaces. Schwartz recently proved that his construction parametrizes the boundary of a connected component of Anosov representations in a certain moduli space of representations of PSL(2,Z) into Isom(SL(3,R)/SO(3)). Weisman. This is joint work in progress with W. Dimoune.

3c972f7a7651e0fe.title: Skein and Hall algebras of decorated marked surfaces
3c972f7a7651e0fe.speaker: Shunsuke KANO
3c972f7a7651e0fe.abstract:
The skein algebra of a surface S is defined using isotopy classes of curves in the thickened surface SxI, where I is the unit interval, subject to local relations involving crossings and their smoothings. Qiu pioneered the use of decorated marked surfaces as a geometric framework for studying the derived category of the Ginzburg dg algebra associated with a triangulation of a marked surface. In this talk, I will introduce the skein algebra of a triangulated decorated marked surface and discuss its connections with the derived Hall algebra of the perfectly valued derived category of the corresponding Ginzburg dg algebra. This is a report on ongoing joint work with Denis Lyskov.
This talk will take place in hybrid mode at the Instiut Henri Poincaré.

4201edc0ce8aedc6.title: A homotopy-theoretic approach to representation stability
4201edc0ce8aedc6.speaker: Nicolas Guès
4201edc0ce8aedc6.abstract:
In a series of papers from the 2010s, Church, Ellenberg and Farb developed the notion of representation stability, aimed at understanding the asymptotic behavior of natural sequences of representations of the symmetric groups S_n, particularly those arising from homological invariants. Such phenomena typically occur for FI-modules, i.e., functors from FI (the category of finite sets and injections) to abelian groups.
In this talk, I will propose a homotopical refinement of representation stability: a derived version adapted to (co)FI-spaces. This viewpoint sheds light on how the phenomenon of representation stability can arise from the high (co)cartesianity of certain cubical diagrams. With this point of view, I will show how one can deduce polynomial growth results for the homotopy groups of ordered configuration spaces on closed manifolds, recover the best known bounds on their cohomology, and generalize stability results of Palmer concerning moduli spaces of submanifolds.

420f8bb1d8144cf4.title: Diffuse Interface Models and their Sharp Interface Limits
420f8bb1d8144cf4.speaker: Helmut Abels
420f8bb1d8144cf4.abstract:
CANCELED – For personal reasons, Helmut Abels has unfortunately been forced to cancel his seminar. – CANCELED
Speaker: Helmut Abels (Universität Regensburg)
Interfaces separating two or more species or components of a material are omnipresent in applications in the sciences. Nowadays there are two main classes of models to describe interfaces, both from a theoretical and practical point of view: In classical so-called « sharp interface models » the species or components under consideration fill disjoint domains that are separated by lower dimensional surfaces of a certain regularity. On the other hand in « diffuse interface models » a partial mixing of the species or components on a small length scale is taken into account, which leads to an interfacial layer of small but positive thickness. This has the advantage that the interfaces do not need to be resolved explicitly and singularities in the interfaces can be described consistently.
In the first part of the talk we will give an overview of some basic diffuse interface models with applications to material sciences. Moreover, we will discuss some analytic results on the relation between diffuse and sharp interface models, when the interfacial thickness of the diffuse interface tends to zero. The analysis is based on formally matched asymptotic expansions (in a rigorous manner) together with uniform estimates for the linearized operator. In this part we will focus on the Allen-Cahn equation as basic model.
In the second part we will discuss a Navier-Stokes/Allen-Cahn system, which describes the flow of two macroscopically immiscible viscous incompressible fluid, separated by a diffuse interface. We will present some recent results on novel higher-order estimates for the sharp interface limit of this system. With the aid of a suitable weight taking the distance to the interface and the interfacial thickness into account we obtain optimal regularity estimates, which are uniformy in the interfacial thickness. This enables to improve previous convergence results in two space dimensions significantly and extend results to three space dimensions. This is a joint-work with Mingwen Fei, Yadong Liu, and Maximilian Moser.

It relies on two main results of independent interest: a Nash structure theorem for the stable completion of an algebraic curve and a tame descent theorem for abstract open polydiscs.

4b4b6dae159dc939.title: Diameters and box spaces
4b4b6dae159dc939.speaker: Alain Valette
4b4b6dae159dc939.abstract:
Le séminaire d'algèbres d'opérateurs aura lieu à l'IHP le temps du trimestre "algèbres d'opérateurs : approximation, ridigité et dynamique"
Résumé : Consider a sequence $(X_k)_{k>0}$ of finite, connected, d-regular graphs with size going to infinity. It is known that, if $(X_k)_{k>0}$ is an expanding sequence, then the diameter of $X_k$ is exactly logarithmic in the number of vertices of $X_k$. On the opposite, for $0<\alpha \leq 1$, say that $(X_k)_{k>0}$ has property $D_\alpha$ if the diameter of $X_k$ grows at least like $|X_k|^\alpha$: this is a strong form of non-expansion. For a finitely generated, residually finite group $G$, let $(N_k)_{k>0}$ be a filtration of $G$. The box space associated with $(N_k)_{k>0}$ is the sequence of finite Cayley graphs $(Cay(G/N_k,S))_{k>0}$ where $S$ is a fixed finite generating set of $G$. It turns out that property $D_\alpha$ for a box space is related to interesting algebraic properties of $G$, and we will survey results by Breuillard-Tointon, Khukhro-Valette, and Guo-Tointon. Now, assuming that $G$ can be realized as a subgroup of $GL_n(A)$, where $A$ is a unital, commutative ring, we have filtrations given by congruence subgroups, giving rise to arithmetic box spaces. Sometimes the growth of the diameter is more constrained on arithmetic box spaces then on general box spaces, i.e. non-arithmeticity can be detected purely metrically. We will illustrate this with lamplighter groups $L_F:=F\wr\Z$, where $F$ is a finite abelian group. This is joint work with Etienne Grezet.

4d7eec8a6e9177c1.title: Sur les points fixes des sous-groupes de Moy-Prasad dans les représentations admissibles irréductibles de groupes réductifs p-adiques (Travaux en cours avec Marie-France Vignéras et Rachel Ollivier)
4d7eec8a6e9177c1.speaker: Guy Henniart
4d7eec8a6e9177c1.abstract:
Soit p un nombre premier et F une extension finie de Q_p.
Soit G un groupe réductif connexe sur F, et C un corps algébriquement
clos. Dans une C-représentation admissible irréductible π du groupe
G(F), les points fixes par un sous-groupe ouvert K forment un C-espace
vectoriel de dimension finie d(K, π). Si π est de dimension infinie,
il est intéressant de savoir comment d(K, π) croît quand K devient de
plus en plus petit. Par exemple, on peut partir d’un sous-groupe de
Moy-Prasad G_x,r (pour x dans l’immeuble de G sur F et r un nombre
réel positif), et faire croître r. Grâce à des résultats de
Harish-Chandra (1978) et T.-C.Tsai (2025), nous prouvons que si la
caractéristique de C n'est pas p, alors pour tout entier n assez grand,
d(G_x,r+2n, π) a la forme P(p^n), où P est un polynôme à
coefficients rationnels, dépendant de x, r, et π. Nous soupçonnons
que cela reste vrai si C est de caractéristique p, mais seul le cas où
G est GL₂ et F=Q_p est connu. Pour G général, même le cas
particulier où π est la représentation de Steinberg de G(F) est
difficile. Cependant, nous obtenons un résultat asymptotique plus
faible, valable pour tout π. Au passage, nous examinons la condition
que G_x,r soit un pro-p groupe uniforme.

56258b78a2e0566c.title: A mathematical perspective on Transformers
56258b78a2e0566c.speaker: Borjan GESHKOVSKI
56258b78a2e0566c.abstract: Physics has long supplied mathematics with some of its central equations. I will argue that Transformers, the engine of large language models, are becoming a source of the same kind. Starting from raw code, under various scaling assumptions, one can interpret Transformers as an interacting particle system in continuous time; tools from PDE and kinetic theory then explain empirically observed phenomena such as representation collapse and “lost in the middle”. Unlike in physics, however, the laws here are designed rather than given, so mathematical understanding can be written back into the architecture. I will close with some thoughts on what this two-way exchange means for applied mathematics.
56258b78a2e0566c.organizer: G. Franz, L. Hauswirth, P. Laurain, R. Petrides, R. Souam

565a9a9df1453759.title: Singularities of the critical wave equation and the Keller-Segel system formed by the collision of collapsing solitons at a point
565a9a9df1453759.speaker: Charles Collot
565a9a9df1453759.abstract: Critical evolution PDEs may have solutions forming a singularity in finite time with anomalous self-similarity. There are now numerous examples where a soliton (here a stationary state or a traveling wave) collapses at a point due to its interactions with the remainder of the solution. Much less is known about singularities formed by several solitons collapsing simultaneously at a single point, especially in the non-radial case. The first example was constructed for the nonlinear Schrodinger equation by Martel-Raphael [Ann. Sci. ENS 2018]. I will present examples of such solutions for the parabolic-elliptic Keller-Segel system in two dimensions [joint work with Ghoul-Masmoudi-Nguyen 2024] and for the cubic wave equation in four dimensions [ongoing joint work with Li to appear]. The associated patterns are caused by different effects for each equation: the solitons' own dynamics, their interactions, and their interactions with the remainder of the solution which is affected by the presence of the multiple nearby potentials from the solitons. I will present ideas for the construction of an approximate solution, and its stability analysis based on the control of its modulating parameters and of suitable norms for the remainder, adapted to the multiscale feature of the problem.

56b6da91a344dc66.title: Compilation of pattern-matching by small inversion
56b6da91a344dc66.speaker: W. Ait Moussa
56b6da91a344dc66.abstract:
Dependent inductive data types are an essential part of type theory based proof-assistant, where they close the gap between theorem proving and functional programming. Their meaning and computational behavior are given by dependent recursors, but those are tedious and unintuitive to work with in a dependent setting. Today, the established practice in dependent settings is to have an expressive high-level dependent pattern matching construct with the same logical power as recursors but which is more natural to work with.
This talk will be split into three parts. First, I will go over the history and established theory of dependent-pattern matching and its correspondence to recursors. Then I will present an alternative translation of the non-recursive part of pattern matching to recursors using small-inversion. Finally, I will present an implementation for Rocq of the latter, written by Thierry Martinez a few years back ; in addition to its value as a basis for a specification for this translation, of particular interest is its extensive use of Ocaml's GADTs in order to formalize a notion of intrinsically well-formed Rocq terms.

617e37ed31495779.title: Formes normales et structures géométriques sur les variétés de Hopf
617e37ed31495779.speaker: Paul Boureau
617e37ed31495779.abstract:
Nous montrerons comment la dynamique holomorphe contractante définissant
une variété de Hopf permet de construire naturellement une géométrie localement homogène.
La théorie de Poincaré–Dulac et les polynômes sous-résonnants conduisent à l’existence
d’une (G,Cn)(G,\mathbb C^n)-structure sur toute variété de Hopf de dimension au moins deux.
Nous étudierons également la rigidité, la non-unicité et la classification de ces structures.

628df6c4380c2afa.title: FAMED triangulations will live forever
628df6c4380c2afa.speaker: Antonin Guilloux
628df6c4380c2afa.abstract:
I will present a joint work with Fathi Ben Aribi and Ka Ho Wong around volume conjectures. Roughly, a volume conjecture describes a link between the semiclassical limit of a quantum invariant of a triangulated hyperbolic knot complement and the hyperbolic geometry of its complement. There are several flavors and we will focus of a version by Andersen and Kashaev.
Recently, arguments by Fathi and Ka Ho reduce essentially this conjecture to a combinatorial property of the triangulation, called FAMED. I will explain this condition and how to extensively test this condition, and a path toward a proof of the volume conjecture.

656fc67ff9721de6.title: Invariant sets of the double Hilbert transform
656fc67ff9721de6.speaker: Alexei Poltoratski
656fc67ff9721de6.abstract: We study planar sets whose indicator functions are invariant under the double Hilbert transform. In the talk we will also mention connections with Sylvester–Gallai configurations, tomography, and superpositions of traveling waves. This is joint work with E. Abakumov, K. Domelevo and S. Petermichl.

666f57fe59a1da30.title: À propos de la tessellation de Poisson-Delaunay : quelques techniques classiques et de nouveaux résultats de loi
666f57fe59a1da30.speaker: Cecilia d'Errico
666f57fe59a1da30.abstract:
Dans cet exposé, nous présentons la tessellation de Delaunay issue d’un processus ponctuel de Poisson homogène sur Rd. Dans une première partie, nous parlerons de la cellule typique et montrerons comment obtenir sa loi à l’aide d’une technique 'combo'
classique : la formule de Mecke + changement de variable de Blaschke-Petkantschin. Dans la deuxième partie, nous étudions le volume de cette cellule : nous voyons comment obtenir ses moments, puis nous résolvons le problème des moments pour déterminer la loi
du volume de la cellule typique. Enfin, nous présenterons d’autres résultats de loi de fonctionnelles de la cellule typique que nous avons obtenus en étendant ces techniques.

66e2752f075b4eff.title: Topological freeness for minimal actions of groups with the rapid decay property
66e2752f075b4eff.speaker: Joseph Gondek
66e2752f075b4eff.abstract: We apply an operator-algebraic property of finitely generated groups, called rapid decay (RD), to topological dynamics. The class of groups with RD includes the hyperbolic groups and cocompact lattices in SL3(R), among many other examples. We show that the compact, minimal G-spaces of an RD group G with amenable neighbourhood stabilizers have some rigidity properties; under general conditions, all such actions are topologically free. 67c0840d946bbf68.title: Proliferation Transitions for Non-Abelian Anyons
67c0840d946bbf68.speaker: Andrea Antinucci
67c0840d946bbf68.abstract:
Phases of matter and the transitions between them are famously characterized within the Landau paradigm and Landau–Ginzburg theory: phases are labeled by broken or unbroken symmetries, while phase transitions are described in terms of scalar order parameters. There are, however, phases beyond the standard Landau paradigm that are distinguished not by the realization of ordinary symmetries, but by that of generalized global symmetries. Among these, topologically ordered phases in (2+1)d possess non-invertible 1-form symmetries described by anyon lines. In this talk, I will present a framework for describing transitions between topologically ordered phases related by anyon proliferation, which can be viewed as a non-invertible generalization of the choice of the unbroken symmetry. The resulting theories involve scalar fields coupled to gauge fields. A crucial ingredient in this construction is the (3+1)d Symmetry Topological Field Theory (SymTFT), which allows to separate symmetry from dynamics and will be employed in a rather unconventional way.

69aa1cc5302c19af.title: Dynamique des tourbillons visqueux dans un demi-plan
69aa1cc5302c19af.speaker: Thierry Gallay
69aa1cc5302c19af.abstract:
Speaker: Thierry Gallay (Université Grenoble Alpes)
Le but de cet exposé est de définir un cadre mathématique permettant de décrire les interactions entre tourbillons et parois pour des écoulements plans à grand nombre de Reynolds. Les phénomènes typiques que l’on souhaite étudier à terme sont le mouvement auto-induit (pour un tourbillon isolé) et l’effet de rebond (pour une paire de tourbillons).
Dans la première partie, à caractère tout à fait élémentaire, on explique comment résoudre les équations de Navier-Stokes incompressibles dans un demi-plan en exploitant l’équation d’évolution pour le tourbillon du fluide. Si l’on suppose que la vitesse s’annule sur la paroi, le tourbillon vérifie une condition au bord non linéaire et non locale qui est difficilement utilisable en pratique. On peut toutefois la remplacer par une condition intégrale permettant une formulation élégante du système, lequel se résout alors par un simple argument de point fixe dans un cadre fonctionnel approprié.
Dans la seconde partie, en cohérence avec l’objectif affiché, on suppose que la donnée initiale est une collection finie de tourbillons ponctuels, dont les circulations peuvent être arbitrairement grandes. Ce cas ne peut pas être traité comme précédemment par un simple argument de point fixe, mais on peut tout de même montrer l’existence et l’unicité de la solution en utilisant une décomposition appropriée, qui permet de traiter la partie la plus singulière de la solution dans le plan tout entier où l’on dispose d’outils plus affûtés. En fonction du temps disponible, on présentera également quelques résultats concernant le comportement asymptotique en temps de la solution, ses propriétés de localisation, ou la question difficile de la limite non visqueuse.
Cet exposé repose entièrement sur un travail en collaboration avec Anne-Laure Dalibard.
Thierry Gallay (Université Grenoble Alpes)

702c137c490164b6.title: What does it mean to formalize a proof? Can we really trust a formalized proof, even if written by an LLM?
702c137c490164b6.speaker: Riccardo BRASCA
702c137c490164b6.abstract: Formalization of mathematics began in the 1970s with various goals. Verifying the correctness of proofs was only one of them and, for most researchers, not the most important. With the rise of AI-assisted and AI-generated proofs, however, the need for reliable verification tools has become increasingly important. In this talk, we will use examples from differential geometry and other areas to explain what it means for a proof to be formalized, whether by a human or by a large language model. We will explain which problems formalization can, and cannot, solve. Finally, we will discuss its role in recent announcements, including the claimed solution to the Navier–Stokes problem.

72002ba2e502d205.title: Algèbres de von Neumann de réseaux arithmétiques et ensembles de Kakeya
72002ba2e502d205.speaker: Mikael de la Salle
72002ba2e502d205.abstract:
Une forme de la conjecture de rigidité de Connes prédit que les algèbres de von Neumann de $\mathrm{PSL_n}(Z)$ sont toutes distinctes. Au moment où j'écris ces lignes, cette conjecture est toujours ouverte. Des anciens travaux avec Vincent Lafforgue et Tim de Laat (ainsi que d'autres travaux de Uffe Haagerup et Tim de Laat) suggèrent une approche possible à cette conjecture, en terme de propriétés d'approximation.
J'expliquerai pourquoi cette approche est difficile: elle implique aussi une forme de la conjecture de Kakeya en toute dimension.
La conjecture de Kakeya en dimension d affirme que toute partie de l'espace euclidien de dimension d, qui contient un segment dans toute direction, est de dimension de Hausdorff égale à d. Au moment où j'écris ces lignes, cette conjecture est prouvée uniquement en dimension 2 (Davies, Cordoba) et 3 (Wang et Zahl).
Café culturel par Amaury Freslon à 13h05 en 2L8.

75ff18b604345dc7.title: Finiteness and density problems for (positive) integral points on Mordell–Schinzel surfaces
75ff18b604345dc7.speaker: Robin Zhang
75ff18b604345dc7.abstract: In 1952, Mordell erroneously claimed that the surface $xyz = G(x,y)$ has infinitely many integral points for any $G \in \mathbb{Z}[x,y]$. I will discuss a classification for finiteness and Zariski density of (positive) integral points on these log K3 surfaces when the coefficients of $G$ are non-negative. This combines a dynamical argument proposed by Mordell, the theory of generalized cluster algebras, and the Killing–Cartan classification of semisimple Lie algebras. This talk is partially based on joint work with Antoine de Saint Germain.

772d2a8890f92411.title: Anti-classification results in dynamical systems
772d2a8890f92411.speaker: Matthew Foreman
772d2a8890f92411.abstract:
Thematic 3-weeks programme at the Institut Henri Poincaré, Paris, May 18th to June 4th, 2027.
Beware: It was reported to us that scammers are sending to participants fraudulent e-mails about accommodation/fees. Please be particularly cautious about e-mails not coming from the organisers nor from an @ihp.fr address.
REGISTRATION IS FREE, HOWEVER MANDATORY.
Presentation of the programme
In recent years, there have been major advances using techniques from Descriptive Set Theory to show, in a rigorous way, that many classical problems in Dynamical Systems are impossible to solve. In this context, a problem that can be set in a Polish space is said to be impossible to solve if it cannot be settled using inherently countable techniques. These groundbreaking results mostly lie in Ergodic Theory, with further significant advances in Topological and Smooth Dynamical Systems.
One main goal of this program is to further enhance interactions between Descriptive Set Theory and Dynamical Systems. It brings together researchers from different fields to settle some of the most famous problems in dynamics dating to the mid-20th century.
A second main goal is to expand applications of the techniques from Descriptive Set Theory to other areas of mathematics.
Week 1
The program begins with lectures introducing the basic impossibility techniques and lectures explaining fundamental concepts in areas of potential applications.
We plan to have tutorials on:
Impossibility Results
Ergodic Theory
Symbolic Dynamics
Smooth Dynamical Systems
Additionally, there will be Research talks and Expository Lectures (primarily in Ergodic Theory and Descriptive Set Theory).
Week 2
Research talks in Descriptive Set Theory, Ergodic Theory, Smooth and Symbolic Dynamics, as well as Expository Lectures, including on:
Impossibility Results in Ergodic theory
Complexity Theory
Flexibility and Rigidity
Moreover, we will have Problem and Discussion Sessions.
Week 3
Topical Days (particularly Complex Dynamics with tutorial); Problem Sessions

81f5130d919a8aaf.title: On supercuspidal representations in the l-adic cohomology of some local Shimura varieties
81f5130d919a8aaf.speaker: Yoichi Mieda
81f5130d919a8aaf.abstract: A local Shimura variety is a p-adic analogue of a Shimura variety. Its l-adic cohomology is expected to be related to the local Langlands correspondence. In the Lubin-Tate case, a supercuspidal representation appears only in the middle degree. In the GSp(4) case, a supercuspidal representation appears only in the degrees 3,4, and it appears in the degree 4 if and only if its L-parameter has non-trivial SL(2)-part. In this talk, I will explain my recent results in this direction for more general cases.

8342a404054eacb7.title: Lissage par peignes et trivialité locale pour les espaces homogènes au-dessus d’une courbe relative
8342a404054eacb7.speaker: Margot Bruneaux
8342a404054eacb7.abstract:
Soit $R$ un anneau local hensélien, de corps résiduel $\kappa$, soit $C$ une courbe projective lisse sur $R$, à fibres géométriquement connexes, soit $G$ un $C$-groupe réductif dont le tore radical $\operatorname{rad}(G)$ est isotrivial, et soit $E\to C$ un $G$-torseur.
Nous montrons que, si le noyau de l'isogénie centrale
\[
G_{\mathrm{sc}}\times_C \operatorname{rad}(G)\longrightarrow G
\]
est étale sur $C$, ou bien si $\kappa$ est un corps suffisamment grand, alors la trivialité de $E_\kappa\to C_\kappa$ pour la topologie de Zariski implique la trivialité de $E\to C$ pour cette même topologie.
Nous démontrons également une version « moyennée » de ce résultat, en supposant seulement que $\operatorname{rad}(G)$ est isotrivial, ainsi qu'une variante concernant les espaces homogènes projectifs, sans aucune hypothèse restrictive sur $G$.
Ces résultats ont notamment pour conséquences un principe local-global pour les torseurs sur les corps de fonctions de courbes au-dessus d'anneaux de valuation discrète henséliens, renforçant des travaux de Gille--Parimala--Suresh, ainsi qu'une version hensélienne d'un théorème de Drinfeld--Simpson.
Nos démonstrations sont de nature géométrique. Elles reposent sur des compactifications de torseurs et sur une technique de lissage par peignes, dans une version relative et arithmétique que nous développons en détail, en nous appuyant sur les travaux de Kollár et de Graber--Harris--Starr.
En collaboration avec Federico Scavia.

83b6ce1f8bc4646c.title: Dynamique de Aut(F_n) sur G^n, pour G compact et n grand
83b6ce1f8bc4646c.speaker: Florestan Martin-Baillon
83b6ce1f8bc4646c.abstract:
Donnons nous un groupe de Lie compact G et un entier n.
Un n-uplet (g_1, …, g_n) étant donné, on peut changer l’un des g_i en son inverse, ou multiplier l’un des
g_i par g_j (avec j différent de i) : ces opérations élémentaires ne changent pas le sous-groupe de G
engendré par les g_i. Ces opérations engendrent un groupe de difféomorphismes de G^n, et le problème
que nous aborderons est d’étudier la dynamique de ce groupe. Pour n suffisamment grand, nous verrons
qu’il est possible de classer les fermés et les mesures invariants.

86e7c3606d9ebbed.title: Sard’s theorem in infinite dimension: from real algebraic geometry to sub-Riemannian geometry
86e7c3606d9ebbed.speaker: Antonio Lerario
86e7c3606d9ebbed.abstract:
Sard’s theorem can fail in infinite dimension, even for polynomial maps with finite-dimensional targets. I will explain how quantitative estimates in real algebraic geometry, combined with finite-dimensional approximation, yield Sard criteria in this setting. I will then show how Kupka’s classical counterexample can be realized inside a sub-Riemannian endpoint map. This produces a smooth bracket-generating distribution whose endpoint map has no regular values, disproving the sub-Riemannian Sard conjecture in the smooth category.
Based on joint works with Luca Rizzi and Daniele Tiberio.

892203e7a7e511fe.title: Nonrelativistic Conformal Collider Physics of Multiparticle Point Production
892203e7a7e511fe.speaker: Dam Thanh Son
892203e7a7e511fe.abstract:
Motivated by nuclear experiments where a few neutrons are produced by a local source, we develop a formalism of "nonrelativistic conformal collider physics." We define detector operators in the nonrelativistic conformal field theory describing fermions at unitarity. We reduce the problem of computing the momentum distribution and correlation between final particles produced by a local source ("point-produced") to the computation of correlation functions involving the detector operators. The general formalism is applied to the point production of three unitary fermions, where we find the momentum and angular distribution of final particles, and point production of a large number of fermions. We discuss a nonrelativistic version of celestial holography, which maps the asymptotic out-state to a quantum wave function in the so-called "oscillator frame." Based on arXiv:2608.18202 with Cyuan-Han Chang, Subham Dutta Chowdhury, and Ian Moult.

8d298e1a3ee4f7d4.abstract:

Deadline for financial support request is October 15, 2026
Recent trends at the interface between information theory, probability, statistics and high-dimensional geometry raise new questions on the role and importance of entropy in the understanding of both asymptotic and finite range phenomena, in particular towards discrete structures and applications to areas such as quantum information, percolation and random matrices. Recent fruitful developments warrant imminent blossom of new ideas and results in this area in the near future.
Another central theme at the interface of High-Dimensional Probability and Convexity is the study of isoperimetric properties of log-concave measures (including isoperimetric-type questions related to convex bodies). This is not a mere curiosity: convexity and isoperimetry play an important role in the study of concentration of measure phenomena which is crucial for harnessing various high-dimensional effects in Probability as well as several applied fields.
The scope of the semester includes developing further connections between Information Theory and Convexity, in all of the different directions described above. The semester will aim to strengthen these powerful interdisciplinary methods, aiming towards challenging issues and applications, including the isoperimetry questions for log-concave measures, and super-concentration properties of models from random matrix theory and statistical mechanics.
The semester’s objective is to foster cross-fertilization between probability, analysis, information theory and convex geometry (continuous and discrete). By organizing two thematic pre-schools, we will ensure active participation by junior researchers, which should have a lasting effect on their careers, as well as influence the routes along which these research areas will be developed in the future. Our two workshops will further provide opportunities for many re- searchers from across the globe to interact and collaborate. We believe that close interactions between these disciplines are a necessary condition to address many mathematical challenges raised in the last decades, and that the timing is optimal to bring together all these powerful ideas which have been recently developed in several communities. Therefore, our proposed semester program will have a strong and lasting impact on High-Dimensional Probability, Convexity and Analysis as a whole.

8d84ab4ce9c180c9.title: On “Siegel Domains” in p-adic Period Spaces
8d84ab4ce9c180c9.speaker: Yoichi Mieda
8d84ab4ce9c180c9.abstract:
Séminaire de géométrie arithmétique
A Siegel domain is a finite-volume subset of a symmetric space whose translates under the action of the relevant arithmetic group cover the entire space. In this talk, we consider an analogue for the p-adic period spaces introduced by Rapoport and Zink. We give a partial criterion for the existence of a Siegel domain and discuss its expected applications.

8de6607c53900f8d.title: Torus actions on compactified braid varieties and polytopality of subword complexes
8de6607c53900f8d.speaker: Mikhail Gorsky
8de6607c53900f8d.abstract:
Every cluster variety admits a faithful regular group action scaling all cluster variables. Given a partial compactification of a cluster variety, a natural question is whether this action extends to a regular action on the compactification. I will explain that, in the case of braid varieties for simple Lie groups, the answer is affirmative for brick compactifications. If the braid variety is an open Richardson variety in the flag variety, the same result holds for the corresponding closed Richardson variety. In the latter case, the faithfully acting group is a torus of rank the Kazhdan-Lusztig d-invariant. The same result holds for projected Richardson varieties. I will also explain that, in general, a braid variety is a torus if and only if each of its brick compactifications is a toric variety with respect to this extended action, if and only if the polar dual of the moment polytope for this action realizes the corresponding subword complex. The braid words satisfying this property turn out to be precisely the double root free words of V. Pilaud and C. Stump. This provides a novel approach to the longstanding open question of the polytopality of spherical subword complexes asked by A. Knutson and E. Miller in 2004, and in particular gives infinite families of subword complexes admitting polytopal realizations in dimension higher than the rank of the corresponding Coxeter group. The talk is based on joint work with Lara Bossinger and José Simental, arXiv:2609.12414.
This talk will take place in hybrid mode at the Institut Henri Poincaré.

Operator algebras are self-adjoint subalgebras of the bounded operators on a Hilbert space and divide into two main classes: C∗-algebras and von Neumann algebras, according to whether one demands that they are closed in the norm topology or the weak operator topology. When one first meets these algebras, they might look quite similar, but they have different natures as exemplified by the commutative case: via the Gelfand transform, abelian C∗-algebras are algebras of continuous functions vanishing at infinity on a locally compact Hausdorff space, while abelian von Neumann algebras are essentially bounded measurable functions on a measure space. These flavours persist in general. Topological concepts such as dimension and invariants such as K-theory pervade the study of C∗-algebras, while measure-theoretic style methods are often used to study von Neumann algebras.
The long thematic program OA will focus on operator algebras and its still evolving interactions with ergodic theory, topological dynamics, discrete subgroups of semisimple Lie groups, analytic, ergodic and geometric group theory, quantum information theory and random matrices.

8f10de0ff45c5eb1.title: Un degré de différentiabilité peut tout changer
8f10de0ff45c5eb1.speaker: Hélène Eynard-Bontemps
8f10de0ff45c5eb1.abstract:
Par lisse, certains entendent de classe $C^1$, d’autres $C^\infty$, alors que pour l’analyse élémentaire, la mécanique Newtonienne ou les questions de courbure, $C^2$ semble plus naturel… Les mathématiques regorgent d’exemples de problèmes ou de techniques qui sont extrêmement sensibles à la régularité dans laquelle on travaille, souvent pour des raisons profondes et intéressantes. J’illustrerai cette affirmation à l’aide d’exemples tirés de la dynamique unidimensionnelle (qui s’intéresse aux difféomorphismes de l’intervalle et du cercle) mais aux origines bien géométriques : le célèbre théorème de Denjoy et le bijou moins connu qu’est le lemme de Nancy Kopell.

934cdfe8c21f0d30.abstract:
This is a thematic trimester programme with short courses, seminars and workshops on Kinetic theory: from long-range interactions to turbulence and quantum simulators.
January 18 to April 9, 2027 at the Institut Henri Poincaré, Paris
REGISTRATION IS MANDATORY AND FREE
IMPORTANT WARNING: Scam / Phishing / SMiShing! Note that ill-intentioned people may be trying to contact some of participants by email or phone to get money and personal details, by pretending to be part of the staff of the conference center. IHP and the organizers will NEVER contact you by phone on this issue and will NEVER ask you to pay for accommodation/ board / possible registration fee in advance.
Deadline for financial support request has been extended to: June 30th, 2026.
Summary
The program centers on the development of a unified understanding of kinetic theory in systems with long‑range interactions, with a particular emphasis on the quantum regime. Long‑range interacting quantum systems—realized experimentally in cold atoms, trapped ions, and polar molecules—exhibit rich dynamical behavior such as metastability, collisionless dynamics, anomalous transport, critical scaling, and turbulence‑like phenomena. These effects are often linked to the Vlasov equation, the collisionless kinetic equation that emerges in the thermodynamic limit. While Vlasov theory is conceptually well established in classical plasma physics, its systematic extension to quantum many‑body systems remains incomplete.
A key scientific motivation of the program is that different communities—mathematical physics, quantum many‑body theory, and AMO physics—address similar non‑equilibrium long‑range phenomena using different methods, preventing the emergence of a unified framework. The program aims to bridge these approaches and clarify conceptual connections between classical and quantum kinetic theories.
The scientific agenda spans several interconnected themes. One major theme is the analysis of classical transport, Vlasov dynamics, and their differences from Boltzmann kinetic theory, including how turbulence, chaos, and long‑range correlations emerge in classical systems. Another theme concerns the quantum generalizations of Vlasov theory, focusing on rigorous derivations and effective equations for quantum gases, including mean‑field and Gross–Pitaevskii limits, and the treatment of finite‑size effects in quantum simulators.
The program will explore non‑equilibrium many‑body dynamics in quantum systems, including quantum turbulence, cascade processes, ergodicity breaking, and anomalous scaling. A related line of inquiry concerns the dynamics of quantum correlations and entanglement, the onset of quantum chaos, and the characterization of universal quasi‑static dynamics in isolated systems. Another scientific direction is the study of effective theories in quantum matter, connecting renormalisation‑group methods with kinetic descriptions and identifying the regimes where classical scaling concepts can illuminate quantum behavior.
On the mathematical side, the program emphasizes rigorous derivations of macroscopic equations from microscopic many‑body dynamics, particularly in long‑range systems, and the formulation of effective transport equations, scaling limits, and mean‑field theories. Renormalisation‑group tools are highlighted both in their rigorous and approximate forms, with the aim of connecting microscopic models to emergent large‑scale behavior in many‑body systems.
Finally, the proposal identifies a scientific need to synthesize current insights into a coherent and predictive quantum kinetic theory for long‑range interactions, and to outline a roadmap of open problems invol

95db7503a93ba418.title: Defects in skein theory
95db7503a93ba418.speaker: Juan Ramón Gómez García
95db7503a93ba418.abstract:
Skein theory forms a once-extended categorified TQFT that assigns skein algebras to surfaces and skein modules to 3-manifolds.
These algebras and modules are defined in terms of generators of topological flavor, namely a certain class of graphs embedded in the 3-manifold,
modulo the relations induced by evaluating (locally) these graphs in an underlying ribbon category. In this talk I will explain how this picture
can be extended to stratified manifolds with strata of codimension 1 and 2 (called defects). Using the appropriate algebraic structures,
we can define evaluation functors around defects, yielding notions of stratified skein modules and algebras. Examples of these structures
are provided by the formalism of parabolic restriction. As an application, we use an interpolating version of parabolic defects to construct
a categorification of the Turaev coproduct in the HOMFLY skein algebra.

970c7dbfcd1f9463.title: Colloquium : "Nielsen meets Weil"
970c7dbfcd1f9463.speaker: Maxim Kontsevich
970c7dbfcd1f9463.abstract: A hundred years ago Jacob Nielsen proposed a lower bound on the number of fixed points of a self-map, utilizing the action on the fundamental group. The natural bookkeeping device is the Reidemeister trace, a linear combination of twisted conjugacy classes. I will review the classical theory and propose an analogue for varieties over finite fields, in the spirit of the rationality part of the Weil conjectures, where the self-map is replaced by the Frobenius automorphism. The resulting conjecture can be checked in non-trivial examples.

9817b8cf32f5e5d2.title: On the undecidability of the QWEP for C*-algebras
9817b8cf32f5e5d2.speaker: Isaac Goldring
9817b8cf32f5e5d2.abstract: In his landmark 1993 paper, Kirchberg introduced a property of C*-algebras called the QWEP, which stands for “quotient of the weak expectation property”. As the name suggests, the property is defined by the fact that the algebra is a quotient of a C*-algebra with the weak expectation property, which was a property introduced by Lance years earlier in connection with the theory of tensor products of C*-algebras. While at first glance this seems to be a strange property, Kirchberg showed that whether or not every C*-algebra has the QWEP is equivalent to the famous Connes Embedding Problem (CEP) from von Neumann algebra theory. The CEP remained open for nearly 50 years until its recent refutation in 2020 via a result in quantum complexity theory (as well as the equivalence with Kirchberg’s QWEP conjecture). Several years ago, I showed that the QWEP is an axiomatizable property of C*-algebras. In this talk, I will present joint work with Aruseelan and Hart where we show that the QWEP does not have an effective axiomatization and, in fact, there can be no effectively axiomatizable satisfiable theory of C*-algebras all of whose models have the QWEP (modulo some nontrivially conditions). The proofs uses the connection with the quantum complexity results mentioned above as well as other techniques from C*-algebra theory. No prior knowledge of continuous logic, operator algebras, or quantum complexity will be assumed.

9a45aa9c03af67e7.title: On the Wasserstein Geodesic Principal Component Analysis of probability measures
9a45aa9c03af67e7.speaker: Alice Le Brigant
9a45aa9c03af67e7.abstract:
The GdT OT-PDE-ML is a research seminar organized by the ParMA team. It brings together researchers to discuss recent theoretical and numerical developments at the crossroads of Optimal Transport theory, Partial Differential Equations and Machine Learning.
Abstract: In this talk we discuss how to perform Principal Component Analysis (PCA) of a dataset whose elements are probability distributions, compared using the Wasserstein distance. The goal is to identify geodesic curves in the space of probability measures that best capture the modes of variation of the underlying dataset. To achieve this, we leverage the Riemannian interpretation of the Wasserstein metric. We first address the case of a collection of centered Gaussian distributions, and show how to lift the computations in the space of invertible linear maps using Bures-Wasserstein geometry. For the more general setting of absolutely continuous probability measures, we use Otto-Wasserstein geometry and neural networks to parameterize geodesics in Wasserstein space. Finally, we compare to classical tangent PCA through various examples and provide illustrations on real-world datasets.

9f79361b0f0772b7.title: De la modélisation aux problèmes inverses : une méthodologie pour les systèmes dynamiques en biomédecine.
9f79361b0f0772b7.speaker: Pierre Monmarché
9f79361b0f0772b7.abstract:
Oratrice : Annabelle Collin (Université de Nantes)
Résumé : Les systèmes dynamiques constituent un cadre naturel pour décrire l'évolution temporelle et spatiale de nombreux phénomènes rencontrés en biologie, et en médecine. Qu'ils soient formulés sous la forme d'équations différentielles ordinaires (EDO) ou d'équations aux dérivées partielles (EDP), ces modèles permettent de formaliser des mécanismes biologiques, physiologiques ou épidémiologiques et d'étudier leur dynamique.
Dans cet exposé, nous présenterons les principales étapes d'une démarche de modélisation mathématique appliquée à des problématiques biomédicales : construction et formalisation du modèle, étude de ses propriétés théoriques, approximation numérique, puis confrontation du modèle aux données à travers la résolution de problèmes inverses. Une attention particulière sera portée à l'estimation de paramètres et d'états non directement observables, ainsi qu'aux difficultés associées à l'identifiabilité, aux incertitudes et au caractère potentiellement bruité ou incomplet des observations.
Nous nous intéresserons plus particulièrement aux approches séquentielles, qui permettent de mettre à jour progressivement l'estimation de l'état du système et de ses paramètres au fur et à mesure de l'acquisition de nouvelles données.
Cette démarche sera illustrée sur un exemple volontairement simple, permettant de mettre en évidence les principales étapes méthodologiques tout en montrant comment des modèles relativement parcimonieux peuvent déjà conduire à des résultats quantitatifs pertinents et exploitables dans un contexte de santé publique.
Retransmission : https://www.ihp.fr/fr/live-0
Tous les séminaires Math Park : https://indico.math.cnrs.fr/category/533/

a30b364eaa318fa2.title: ProofTree: Structured Representations for Human-Centred Mathematical Exploration
a30b364eaa318fa2.speaker: Carl Jontza
a30b364eaa318fa2.abstract:
If formal proofs become abundant, how can we help people find mathematics they care about and explore it in ways that are understandable and engaging? I will present ongoing work on ProofTree, investigating a persistent, versioned graph of goals, assumptions, and alternative arguments as an intermediate representation connecting human-readable reasoning with formal proofs. The aim is to support discovery, understanding, and human guidance at levels of abstraction suited to a person’s background, interests, and objectives.
A case study from Lean-based proof hierarchies, involving confusion between an induction hypothesis and a proof obligation, will motivate technical questions about preserving logical scope, revising arguments, and maintaining links to checked proofs. I will discuss what records of exploration should preserve for subsequent reuse, and outline an evaluation agenda that considers mathematical relevance, understanding, and user experience alongside proof completion and human and computational cost.

a329e1844f0ce445.title: Reprojections des pavages par le Spectre et motifs hexagonaux
a329e1844f0ce445.speaker: Arnaud Chéritat
a329e1844f0ce445.abstract: L'une des monotuiles apériodiques découvertes en 2023 par Smith et al. est appelée spectre. On peut associer naturellement aux pavages par le spectre un relevé à $\mathbb{R}^4$ du graphe des arêtes du pavage. On peut faire de même avec un autre graphe, issu d'une décoration particulière de la tuile. En reprojetant ces graphes vers le plan selon différentes directions, on observe des motifs intéressants. J'ai effectué une analyse détaillée de l'un d'entre eux.

a5b13a77b85fcc84.title: Zeta Values as Moments: A Random Matrix Theory
a5b13a77b85fcc84.speaker: Hartmut Monien
a5b13a77b85fcc84.abstract: The values of the Riemann zeta-function $\zeta\left(\alpha+\beta n\right)$ with $\alpha>1$, $\beta>0$ and $n$ a positive integer can be viewed as moments of a probability distribution. In my talk I will construct the corresponding random matrix model and determine its asymptotic spectral curve, which exhibits an unusual feature, the complete asymptotics of its partition function and uniform approximations to its correlation functions using a discrete version of Riemann-Hilbert problem with Airy and Bessel asymptotics. This relates a problem in number theory to ideas of Vershik and Okounkov in the representation theory of the symmetric group.

a9e4d70457516f82.title: Classical Transport and Dynamical Evolution in the Statistical Physics of Long-Range Interaction Systems
a9e4d70457516f82.abstract:
Kinetic theory: from long-range interactions to turbulence and quantum simulators
Workshop 1: Classical Transport and Dynamical Evolution in the Statistical Physics of Long-Range Interaction Systems
March 1 to 5, 2027 - IHP, Paris
Summary
This workshop aims to synthesize established paradigms from classical transport with the overlapping frameworks of quantum dynamics, forging a coherent pathway toward understanding transport phenomena, turbulence, and chaos in strongly correlated quantum matter. Of central observable importance is the interferometric comparison between the mean-field Vlasov description and the collisionally decohered Boltzmann equation—highlighting the nonlocal phase-space structures endemic to long-range interacting systems, in stark contrast with the short-range statistical closures of local theories.

ae962c76bf6437f0.title: Irreducibility of random reciprocal polynomials
ae962c76bf6437f0.speaker: David Hokken
ae962c76bf6437f0.abstract: Let $P = a_m T^m + \sum_{j=0}^{m} a_j (T^{m-j} + T^{m+j})$ be a monic reciprocal polynomial of even degree n, with the $a_j$ drawn independently and uniformly at random from $\{1, 2, \ldots, H\}$ for some fixed integer $H \geq 35$. In joint work with Dimitris Koukoulopoulos, building on prior work of Bary-Soroker—Koukoulopoulos—Kozma, we show that $P$ is irreducible over the rationals, and has large Galois group, with probability tending to 1 as $n$ tends to infinity. This is in line with the long-held belief going back in various forms to Hilbert, Van der Waerden, Odlyzko—Poonen and Konyagin that a typical polynomial is irreducible and has Galois group as large as possible. I will discuss some recent, related developments in the field of probabilistic Galois theory before discussing aspects of the proof, which draws from classical polynomial theory, Fourier analysis, probability theory and group theory.

af9c44e02345c816.title: Dynamical Tidal Response of Neutron Stars from Scattering Amplitudes
af9c44e02345c816.speaker: Muddu Venkata Sai Saketh
af9c44e02345c816.speaker_affiliation: International Centre for Theoretical Sciences (ICTS-TIFR), Bengaluru, India
af9c44e02345c816.abstract:
Séminaire Amplitudes et Gravitation sur l'Yvette (IHES/IPhT)
In this talk I will describe an amplitude-based framework for extracting the frequency-dependent tidal response of neutron stars while preserving the tidal resonances associated with their normal modes. The response is obtained by matching the amplitude for gravitational-wave scattering off a neutron star, equivalently gravitational Compton scattering, computed using relativistic stellar perturbation theory, to the corresponding amplitude in worldline effective field theory. The tidal contribution is isolated through the difference between the neutron-star and black-hole scattering phases. Unlike conventional treatments, the construction allows for a post-Newtonian expansion without Taylor expanding the response in frequency or assuming a harmonic-oscillator model for the internal dynamics.
I will present the tidal response through relative third post-Newtonian (3PN) order and use currently available numerical results to illustrate its frequency dependence. The results reproduce the known static Love numbers in the low-frequency limit, exhibit resonances at the expected stellar mode frequencies, and capture their damping through gravitational-wave emission. I will also discuss the renormalisation of the tidal response required through 3PN order. Time permitting, I will outline how the resulting response can be incorporated into binary dynamics and ultimately into gravitational waveforms.

b029985993a2d7ec.title: Scary Wheels (and Super Shrubs)
b029985993a2d7ec.speaker: Andrei Negut
b029985993a2d7ec.abstract: Together with Alexander Tsymbaliuk, we propose a blueprint for constructing shuffle realizations of various quantum loop (super)algebras; this is a valuable tool for the study of these important algebraic structures and their representation theory. We apply this framework to the case of classical super-types A,B,C,D, which leads us into new combinatorics: higher order wheel conditions on one hand, and on the other hand certain generalizations of Young diagrams that we call shrubs (in types A) and asps (in types B,C,D).

b0f70c00f37651fb.title: A planar model for odd Khovanov homology
b0f70c00f37651fb.speaker: Naageswaran Manikandan
b0f70c00f37651fb.abstract:
In this talk, we will discuss an extension of odd Khovanov homology to tangles. This construction is closely related in spirit to the approach introduced by Bar-Natan for even Khovanov homology. We will first review Bar-Natan's construction for even Khovanov homology and then describe a modification of this framework that produces the odd Khovanov invariant. If time permits, we will also briefly discuss the functorial properties of this construction.
This is a joint work in progress with Shun Ming Samuel Lee and Léo Schelstraete.
